method: fair comparison: each candidate served via llama.cpp --jinja (native tool-call template parsing) at ctx_size 16384 on linux-cpu, driven through the same aegis run -> opencode serve path on the Fib task (real coding task) at a 900s relaxed budget. Tool-call fidelity = the model's tool call executed (file edited), with no native tool markup leaked into message text.
finding: BOTH candidates complete the real task on CPU via llama.cpp --jinja, with correct tool-call parsing (no XML leak). This REVERSES the SERVE-016/019 'qwen3-coder fails on CPU' result, which was a harness artifact: Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint did not parse qwen3-coder's native XML tool calls (<function=...>), so they leaked into text and never executed. Served correctly (--jinja), qwen3-coder completes (208s) and is vindicated as the agentic primary. The earlier comparison was unfair; the production llama.cpp path is fair.
implications: On the llama.cpp production path (MODEL_REF=qwen3-coder), the qwen default is correct and works on CPU.
The Ollama spike still leaks qwen's XML tool calls, so the linux-cpu Ollama default stays gemma (DefaultModelForTarget) until an Ollama tag with a correct tool template + num_ctx is staged.
This is a fair PARSING comparison on CPU; an interactive-latency ranking still wants GPU (SERVE-021).
